headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks from Chatwoot’s inbound content handling; no direct shared-channel evidence for the Spring samples.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot ingests customer messages and integrates with Slack/Dialogflow/Shopify/Linear, so attacker-controlled content can plausibly reach downstream parsers. spring-integration-samples has no documented input surfaces, so the pairwise bridge is inferred rather than observed; uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF Chatwoot forwards untrusted customer text into an automation or parser without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF spring-integration-samples is wired to consume Chatwoot output as instructions, the risk materializes.
mitigations: Disable or restrict automation paths that interpret free-form text.
Add allowlists for commands and structured fields only.
Insert a human review step before any action-taking integration.
Log and flag messages containing instruction-like patterns.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Chatwoot and downstream consumers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while spring-integration-samples shows no data classes or egress. No shared workspace or authenticated principal is documented, so leakage is possible only through an unshown integration path and the blast radius appears limited by the sparse B profile.
conditions: IF both agents are placed in the same workspace or pipeline, Chatwoot data could flow into B.
IF B is extended to read or forward Chatwoot exports, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not mount shared folders containing customer records.
Review outbound integrations in Chatwoot and disable unused ones.
Use redacted test data for any shared pipeline.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot has broad network egress but no filesystem or OAuth write scopes are documented, and spring-integration-samples has no write-capability surfaces or concurrency model. With no overlapping mutable resource documented, a capability conflict pathway is not supported.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same mutable resource, conflict risk would need reassessment.
mitigations: Keep write scopes disjoint.
Avoid shared mutable directories.
Document any future shared resource before enabling it.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can emit customer-facing content and integrate with external systems; if spring-integration-samples consumes that output as authoritative, errors or hallucinated details can cascade into downstream actions. The B profile lacks verification or critical-evaluation behavior, so the interaction is inferred and not directly evidenced, warranting medium rather than low.
conditions: IF B treats Chatwoot output as authoritative without validation, cascading errors can propagate.
IF Chatwoot-generated summaries are used to trigger actions in B, downstream mistakes become operational.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all Chatwoot-derived inputs.
Add a manual approval step before any action-taking.
Compare outputs against source records before use.
Limit B to read-only consumption of Chatwoot data.
requires-engineering: add confidence and provenance metadata to Chatwoot outputs.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, but the profiles do not document residency, certifications, or retention mismatches with spring-integration-samples. Because B shows no data handling or egress, there is no concrete compliance breach pathway beyond an unspecified future integration, so this remains low.
conditions: IF customer data from Chatwoot is routed into a jurisdictionally restricted deployment of B, compliance review is required.
IF B later stores or logs Chatwoot data under a different retention policy, mismatch risk appears.
mitigations: Confirm data residency for any shared deployment.
Disable logging of customer payloads in B.
Align retention settings before connecting the agents.
Use a DPA for any cross-system transfer.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
